chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, who said:
I heard him saying: There is no harm in marrying a Jewish woman or a Christian woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah), while he already has a wife.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim man marry a Jewish or Christian woman for temporary marriage while already having a wife?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies that the general prohibition against temporary marriage with non-Muslims does not apply to Jewish and Christian women, even when the man is already married to a Muslim woman, highlighting the distinct legal status of Ahl al-Kitab in Shia jurisprudence. Scholars note this ruling underscores the permissibility of mut'ah with People of the Book as a specific exception to the broader preference for marrying Muslim women, reflecting the practical flexibility of the genre in early Shia legal thought.
